findings.title: Harvest count and harvested weight are multiplied by the number of journal entries
findings.where: GET /api/plants, GET /api/plants/{id}; Plants list and plant detail pages
findings.steps: Add journal entries to a plant that has harvests (Tomato has 3 harvests totalling 1350 g). Open /plants or GET /api/plants/1.
findings.expected: harvest_count 3, harvest_grams 1350 (1.35 kg), whatever the number of journal entries.
findings.actual: Tomato with 2 journal entries showed harvest_count 6 and harvest_grams 2700. With 3 entries the plants list showed 'Harvested 4.05 kg'. The new LEFT JOIN on journal_entries makes a row for every harvest and journal pair, and COUNT(h.id) and SUM(h.weight_grams) are not de-duplicated.
findings.evidence: curl /api/plants/1 returned harvest_count=6, harvest_grams=2700, but the harvests array has 3 items summing to 1350. The plants list UI showed '4.05 kg' for Tomato.

findings.title: Journal requests have no timeout: a hung request spins forever and the button stays disabled
findings.where: /plants/{id} (Add entry, Save entry, Delete) and the /journal search
findings.steps: Make POST /api/journal hang (never respond), then click 'Add entry'. Separately, on /journal make GET /api/journal hang and type in the search box.
findings.expected: After 10 s the request fails with a visible error and the user can try again.
findings.actual: After 12 s the button still reads 'Saving…' and is disabled. On /journal, 'Loading entries…' stays up with no end, and the old unfiltered results stay on screen under the new query.
findings.evidence: Playwright: submit button text 'Saving…', disabled=true after 12 s. The journal page showed 'Loading entries…' plus stale results 13 s after typing.

findings.title: Journal page error state has no retry
findings.steps: Make GET /api/journal fail (502, HTML body) and type a search term.
findings.expected: An error message with a Retry button that reloads once the server is back.
findings.actual: Only 'Could not load the journal.' is shown. The only way to recover is to edit the search text or reload the page.
findings.evidence: The only button in main was 'Clear search'.

findings.title: Plant detail journal load error has no retry
findings.steps: Make GET /api/journal?plant_id=… return 500 and open a plant from the plants list (or directly).
findings.expected: An error with a Retry button in the journal section.
findings.actual: 'Could not load the journal.' with no retry. The only button in the section is 'Add entry'. The badge still shows the count (for example '3 entries') next to an empty error state.

findings.title: Very large plant_id or entry id gives 500 Internal Server Error
findings.evidence: curl status codes: POST 500, GET 500, PUT 500.

findings.title: Search longer than 80 characters gives a raw validation error instead of a usable message
findings.steps: Type 81 or more characters into Search.
findings.expected: The input limits length (maxlength) or shows a friendly message. Results do not just vanish.
findings.actual: The list is replaced by 'Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters'. The input has no maxlength.

findings.title: Ancient dates are accepted and shown oddly
findings.expected: Reject implausible dates (for example before the plant's planting date or before 1900) with a reason.
findings.evidence: The journal feed showed 'Tomato 1 Jan 1 x'.

findings.title: Retry after a timed-out add creates a duplicate entry
findings.steps: Submit a new entry while the response is lost or slow, then submit again (or reload and resubmit).
findings.actual: There is no idempotency key or dedupe. The first request still lands on the server, so the retry makes a second entry. In testing, the hung 'hang test' POST was later applied server-side.
findings.evidence: The 'hang test' entry appeared after the hung request was released. The code has no idempotency handling.

findings.title: Character counter counts UTF-16 units, not characters
findings.steps: Type emoji into the entry text.
findings.expected: The counter and the 500 limit match the server's limit, which counts characters.
findings.actual: Each emoji counts as 2, so the textarea maxlength stops at about 250 emoji even though the server would accept 500.
findings.evidence: Typing 'Retry test 🌱 x "q"' (25 characters) showed '474 characters left'.

findings.title: Plant detail journal shows only the first 500 entries with no indication
findings.steps: Have more than 500 entries for one plant.
findings.expected: All entries reachable (pagination), or a note that the list is truncated.
findings.actual: The page fetches limit=500 and silently hides older entries, while the badge shows the full count.
findings.evidence: The code requests useApiFetch('/journal', {query:{plant_id, limit:500}}) with no paging.
